- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods, especially when sentiment is >0.6 and recent prices are rising.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes or corrections when sentiment is negative or low (sentiment <0.3).
- Model tends to overreact to recent highs; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast is significantly higher than true outcome 3–5 days later, reduce subsequent forecast by 3–7% to account for momentum decay.
- Avoid “overshoot” after sentiment spikes: if sentiment rises sharply and forecast peaks >15% above prior high, cap forecast at prior high + 5%.
- When sentiment is consistently low (avg <0.4) over 3+ days, reduce forecast by 3–8% to reflect subdued market behavior.
- Forecast should not exceed 15% above recent 10-day average unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.75) and volatility is high.
